About GlobalFoundries
GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power-efficient and high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com.

Internship Program Overview:
Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives.

Summary of Role:
GlobalFoundries (GF) is seeking a summer 2027 intern to support the development of industry-leading electro-optical transceivers using GF's Photonix platform and advanced 2.5D and 3D co-packaged optics form factors. This hands-on role will contribute to thermal, mechanical, electrical, and optical chip-package co-design with a focus on module performance, reliability, packaging design, materials selection, and advanced chiplet integration requirements.

Essential Responsibilities include:

- Support Silicon Photonics advanced packaging innovation and customer design enablement by contributing to packaging design rules, product requirements, and efficient manufacturing processes with internal teams and OSAT ecosystem partners.

- Participate in cross-functional design reviews and use engineering analysis to help resolve technical, manufacturability, reliability, and yield concerns for new customer products.

- Develop and apply analysis or simulation models to evaluate package performance, manufacturability, cost, and quality, and document findings and recommendations for engineering stakeholders.

- Contribute to qualification robustness and continuous improvement plans by applying consistent design processes, tracking requirements, and supporting product development from concept through production readiness.

Other Responsibilities:

- Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.

Required Qualifications:

- Education – Actively pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Photonics, Optical Engineering, Packaging Engineering or a related field through an accredited degree program during the internship.

- Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing.

- Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal).

- Travel - Up to 10%.

- Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Prior related internship, research, or co-op experience in semiconductor packaging, photonics, optics, or advanced electronics.

- Demonstrated leadership experience through academic projects, student organizations, competitions, or prior employment.

- Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making.

- Project management skills and the ability to innovate and execute solutions in ambiguous environments.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills.

- Strong planning and organizational skills.

- Exposure to thermal, mechanical, electrical, optical, or multiphysics simulation tools.

- Knowledge of semiconductor packaging, chiplets, silicon photonics, or co-packaged optics is a plus.

Launch your career in advanced analytics with Vanguard’s College to Corporate (C2C) Internship Program. As a Data Scientist intern, you’ll help apply advanced analytics, machine learning, and AI to solve business problems and support data-driven decision-making. This immersive internship combines real-world project work, mentorship, and structured development to help you strengthen your technical depth, business acumen, and leadership capability in a collaborative, purpose-driven environment.

In this internship you will:

- Support advanced analytics work that helps teams identify patterns, predict outcomes, and improve decision-making at scale.

- Prepare, transform, and analyze data to support machine learning, statistical modeling, and AI-driven solutions.

- Contribute to model development, testing, validation, or experimentation efforts in partnership with data scientists and business stakeholders.

- Help communicate analytical findings, implications, and recommendations in a way that supports business action.

- Gain exposure to applied AI and advanced analytics work, such as automation, model operationalization, and insight generation.

- Build foundational leadership skills by taking ownership of work, collaborating across teams, and contributing ideas in a fast-paced, learning-focused environment.

- Build relationships with program managers, alumni, senior leaders, and peers across the program

- Receive coaching and mentorship from your department manager and program leaders to support your development.

What it takes:

- Enrolled in a master’s degree or PhD program — or advanced graduate study — in Data Science, Analytics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field.

- Strong interest in advanced analytics, machine learning, AI, and using data to solve complex business problems.

- Experience through coursework, research, internships, or projects using tools such as SQL, Python, statistical methods, machine learning libraries, or cloud-based analytics tools.

- Demonstrated leadership skills and/or leadership aspirations.

- Strong analytical, communication, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills.

- Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative, team-oriented environment.

- Cumulative GPA of 3.2 or higher preferred.

Additional Information:

- This program is a full-time, paid 10-week summer internship

- Vanguard is not offering sponsorship for this position

- The start date for this program will be May/June 2027

Sponsorship

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.

Your Impact

As an intern on the Axon Electrical Engineering team, you will gain hands-on experience alongside senior engineers and mentors. You’ll contribute to the design, development, testing, and debugging of cutting-edge electronic circuits that power Axon’s products.

Your academic knowledge and engineering curiosity will be put into practice in real-world applications—from prototyping through validation. You’ll also collaborate with mechanical and software engineers to help bring world-class products to market.

This is your opportunity to deepen your electronics and product design expertise while supporting technologies that positively impact law enforcement, public safety, and the communities they serve.

What You'll Do

- Support the TASER electrical engineering team in designing, developing, testing, debugging, and building new products throughout the development cycle.

- Collaborate with peers and senior engineers to deliver robust electronic designs.

- Develop and execute test plans, define test methods, and validate designs.

- Bring up, characterize, and debug systems and circuits using lab tools (oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers, power supplies, hi-pot testers, etc.).

- Evaluate and document design outcomes and test results; present findings to design teams for review.

- Review product design requirements in relation to system objectives.

- Participate in schematic design of embedded mixed-signal circuits (OrCAD), integrating power supplies, microcontrollers, lighting and display drivers, memory (FLASH/EEPROM), regulators, batteries, high/low-speed interfaces (USB, UART, SPI, I²C), RF transceivers, sensors, and analog/digital components.

- Contribute to PCB design implementations and inspections using Allegro layout tools.

- Engage in design reviews and inspections, offering constructive feedback while learning key design principles.

- Assess circuit performance and verify compliance with product and regulatory requirements.

What You Bring

- College senior majoring in Electrical or Computer Engineering.

- Strong academic performance with a solid engineering foundation.

- Ability to apply classroom knowledge to real-world problems through labs, internships, or projects.

- Knowledge of discrete analog and digital components (RLCs, transistors, diodes, LEDs, voltage regulators, microcontrollers, etc.).

- Experience designing or integrating circuits in one or more areas:

- Hands-on bench experience with oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, etc.

- Ability to read and analyze component datasheets and technical documentation.

- Proficiency with documentation and presentation tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

- Cultural alignment to Axon Company Values: https://global.axon.com/company/values

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience developing embedded hardware systems (capstone, internship, or equivalent) in a cross-functional team (EE/FW/ME).

- Schematic design experience using Cadence/OrCAD Capture or similar tools.

- Understanding of common power supply topologies (buck, boost, buck-boost, LDOs) and their trade-offs.

- Soldering experience for PCB population or component replacement during troubleshooting.

Work Location

This role is based out of our Scottsdale, AZ office and follows a hybrid schedule. We rely on in-person collaboration and ask that team members work onsite Tuesdays through Fridays, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays, unless there is an approved workplace accommodation. We believe that connection fuels innovation, and our in-office culture is designed to foster meaningful teamwork, mentorship, and shared success.

Please Note

- Strive for a full 12 weeks

- Semester interns: May 2027 – August 2027

- Quarter interns: June 2027 – August 2027

The starting hourly pay for this role is USD $35. The actual hourly pay is dependent upon many factors such as: level, function, training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs, geographic market, and often a combination of all these factors. Our benefits offer an array of options to help support you physically, financially and emotionally through the big milestones and in your everyday life. To see more details on our benefits offerings please visit http://www.axon.com/careers/benefits.
